paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus leaves, and He does not leave His people empty-handed. He tells the apostles to wait for "the gift the Father promised," and then He says, "you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you" (Acts 1:4, 8). So the waiting isn't wasted time. It's the oven warming up before the batch goes in.

Now, the apostles want a date. I get it, I peek at the oven door like it owes me money. But Jesus says, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority" (Acts 1:7). The Father holds the calendar, and Jesus hands the apostles a job instead: "you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth" (Acts 1:8). That job reaches you too, baker, so don't spend your day squinting at the sky when there's work in front of you.

And here's the part that keeps my ovens hot. The two men in white say, "This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven" (Acts 1:11). He's the SAME Jesus, and He is coming back. So you wait with hope, you stay ready, and you tell people about Him right where you stand.
